result.title: Sequencing-Free Protospacer-Adjacent Motif Discovery for Uncharacterized CRISPR-Cas9 Orthologs via Active Learning
result.authorString: Kirillov B, Vasileva A, Fedorov O, Kuzmina Y, Kolesnik M, Trofimova A, Demkina A, Ronchikova V, Drozhzhina M, Abramova M, Gorkovskaia A, Malysheva P, Vilinski-Mazur K, Khodorkovskii M, Panov M, Severinov KV.
result.abstractText: Cas9 nucleases, essential components of gene editing, recognize target DNA through a Protospacer-Adjacent Motif (PAM) and cleave only if recognition succeeds. Metagenomic searches and generative protein models currently produce novel CRISPR-Cas9 orthologs at scale, but their adoption in practice is limited by a laborious and data-intensive PAM characterization step which requires exhaustive  in vitro and/or  in vivo screens followed by sequencing. We present a workflow that reduces PAM discovery to a handful of iterative cleavage assays, guided by an active learning algorithm prioritizing the most informative candidate sequences. result.title: "The pharmacological potential of CRISPR-Cas9: Revolutionizing gene therapy and drug development".
result.authorString: Acharyya S, Behera B, Pradhan R, Debata J, Patra PK, Giri S, Kumar HK.
result.abstractText: CRISPR-Cas9 has entered the mainstream of genetic research and therapeutic development, offering a level of programmable and targeted gene editing that has substantially expanded the possibilities of genetic manipulation. This review focuses on the discovery to development of CRISPR-Cas9 and its recent practice in pharmacological and biotechnology field. We discuss further advancements in CRISPR technology such as high-fidelity CRISPR and new systems Cas12 and Cas13 which increases efficiency of editing and opens more opportunities.
